how_to_reproduce: python3 run-edge-r32.py   -> rebuilds a fresh sandbox git repo under this seat's scratch dir, reruns the lane tool over every case exactly as its usage says (cwd = sandbox repo, lane-rev = sandbox commit) and compares the stored `actual` column; --update rewrites that column.
expected_semantics: `expected` is the report required by the primary reading of the quoted rule-text clauses (`rule_text_reading.basis` says which reading and why). `alt_reading` records the competing reading where the clause is ambiguous, with the report that reading requires. `agree` compares actual against `expected`; `agree_alt` compares actual against `alt_reading` (null when there is none).

cases.title: setext heading (Files opened / ---) opens the files-opened block

clauses: 1. A block opens at a Markdown heading (any level) whose text contains `files opened` or `opened files` (case-insensitive), or at a line whose trimmed text starts with `Files opened:` or `Opened files:` (case-insensitive).

2. Entries are the following lines that start (after optional indentation) with `- `, `* `, `+ `, `N. ` or `N) `, or with `|` (a table row); a table's separator row (only `|`, `-`, `:` and spaces) and the row directly above it are not entries. Blank lines inside the block are skipped.

4. An entry's candidates are its tokens, stripped of wrapping backticks, quotes and brackets, trailing `,;.` and a `:L` / `:L-M` suffix, that contain `://`, `/` or `.` or equal `LOG.md`, `SCORECARD.md`, `SKILL.md` or `PROVINCE.md`. An entry with no candidate, or with a candidate no allow line matches, is one `writer-forbidden-opened-path` hit at its own line.
rule_text_reading.reading: Clause 1 opens a block at "a Markdown heading (any level)". A setext heading is a Markdown heading (level 1 with `===`, level 2 with `---`); its text is the line above the underline, here `Files opened`, which contains `files opened`. So the block opens at line 1, the `- ` line is an entry (clause 2) and its candidate `.ufo/waves/round-31/rule-text.md` matches an allow line (clause 4): no hit.

alt_reading.description: Block opener must be an ATX `#` heading at column 0, so the setext heading opens nothing and the brief has no entry in any block (clause 5).

clauses: 1. A block opens at a Markdown heading (any level) whose text contains `files opened` or `opened files` (case-insensitive), or at a line whose trimmed text starts with `Files opened:` or `Opened files:` (case-insensitive).

rule_text_reading.reading: Clause 1 says "a Markdown heading (any level)" with no column-0 qualifier. In CommonMark an ATX heading may be indented by up to three spaces and is still a heading, so the heading text `Files opened` contains `files opened` and the block opens. Clause 2 allows optional indentation before the `- ` marker, so the second line is an entry; clause 4: its candidate matches an allow line. No hit.

alt_reading.description: Only `#` headings at column 0 open a block, so the 2-space indented heading is not seen and the brief has no entry (clause 5).

cases.title: CONTROL: `#` heading indented 4 spaces is an indented code block, not a heading

clauses: 1. A block opens at a Markdown heading (any level) whose text contains `files opened` or `opened files` (case-insensitive), or at a line whose trimmed text starts with `Files opened:` or `Opened files:` (case-insensitive).

2. Entries are the following lines that start (after optional indentation) with `- `, `* `, `+ `, `N. ` or `N) `, or with `|` (a table row); a table's separator row (only `|`, `-`, `:` and spaces) and the row directly above it are not entries. Blank lines inside the block are skipped.
5. A brief with no entry in any block is one `writer-missing-files-opened-list` hit at line 1.
rule_text_reading.reading: Four spaces of indentation makes the line an indented code block in CommonMark, so it is not a heading under any reading and clause 1 opens no block. The brief has no entry in any block, so clause 5 gives one `writer-missing-files-opened-list` hit at line 1. Both the markdown reading and the column-0 reading agree here: this control shows the tool reacts to indentation depth, not to indentation as such.

rule_text_reading.reading: No clause of the rule mentions line terminators, and CRLF is a line terminator, so the brief reads as `## Files opened` / `- .ufo/waves/round-31/rule-text.md`. The heading contains `files opened` (clause 1), the `- ` line is an entry (clause 2) and its candidate token is `.ufo/waves/round-31/rule-text.md`, which matches an allow line (clause 4). No hit.

alt_reading.description: The carriage return stays inside the path token, so the candidate no longer matches the allow line and becomes forbidden.

cases.title: tab directly after `-` is not a list marker

clauses: 1. A block opens at a Markdown heading (any level) whose text contains `files opened` or `opened files` (case-insensitive), or at a line whose trimmed text starts with `Files opened:` or `Opened files:` (case-insensitive).

2. Entries are the following lines that start (after optional indentation) with `- `, `* `, `+ `, `N. ` or `N) `, or with `|` (a table row); a table's separator row (only `|`, `-`, `:` and spaces) and the row directly above it are not entries. Blank lines inside the block are skipped.
3. The block closes at the first heading or at the first other non-blank line.
5. A brief with no entry in any block is one `writer-missing-files-opened-list` hit at line 1.
rule_text_reading.reading: Clause 2 enumerates the entry markers as `- `, `* `, `+ `, `N. `, `N) ` and `|`: the dash is followed by a space, so `-\t/etc/passwd` is not an entry marker and the line is not an entry. Clause 3 then closes the block at that first other non-blank line, so the brief has no entry in any block and clause 5 gives one `writer-missing-files-opened-list` hit at line 1. The path on that line is never inspected as a candidate.

alt_reading.description: A tab is a valid list-item separator in CommonMark, so `-\t/etc/passwd` is a list item and its path is an entry candidate that no allow line matches.

cases.note: Both readings exit 1 but with different rules; the literal reading is the one the clause text supports, SKILL.md names the tab behaviour a known limit.

cases.title: a `../` path passes an allow glob

clauses: 1. A block opens at a Markdown heading (any level) whose text contains `files opened` or `opened files` (case-insensitive), or at a line whose trimmed text starts with `Files opened:` or `Opened files:` (case-insensitive).

2. Entries are the following lines that start (after optional indentation) with `- `, `* `, `+ `, `N. ` or `N) `, or with `|` (a table row); a table's separator row (only `|`, `-`, `:` and spaces) and the row directly above it are not entries. Blank lines inside the block are skipped.

4. An entry with no candidate, or with a candidate no allow line matches, is one `writer-forbidden-opened-path` hit at its own line.
rule_text_reading.reading: Clause 4 says a candidate is forbidden when "no allow line matches" it, and the allow file holds one bash glob per line. The candidate token is the whole `/fast/scratch/hyaku/mori-r32/ExecEdgeFixtures/allowed/../../secret.txt`; the allow line `/fast/scratch/hyaku/mori-r32/ExecEdgeFixtures/allowed/*` matches it (in bash pattern matching `*` also spans `/`). No clause of the rule normalises `..`, so the entry is allowed: no hit.

alt_reading.description: `..` segments are resolved before matching, so the candidate leaves the allowed directory and matches no allow line.

cases.note: Normalised, the candidate is /fast/scratch/hyaku/mori-r32/ExecEdgeFixtures/secret.txt, one level above the allowed/ subtree. SKILL.md names the un-normalised matching a known limit.

cases.title: a `# files opened` line inside a code fence does not open a block

clauses: 1. A block opens at a Markdown heading (any level) whose text contains `files opened` or `opened files` (case-insensitive), or at a line whose trimmed text starts with `Files opened:` or `Opened files:` (case-insensitive).

2. Entries are the following lines that start (after optional indentation) with `- `, `* `, `+ `, `N. ` or `N) `, or with `|` (a table row); a table's separator row (only `|`, `-`, `:` and spaces) and the row directly above it are not entries. Blank lines inside the block are skipped.

4. An entry with no candidate, or with a candidate no allow line matches, is one `writer-forbidden-opened-path` hit at its own line.
rule_text_reading.reading: Clause 1 opens a block at "a Markdown heading". Inside a fenced code block the line `# files opened` is code content, not a heading, so it opens nothing; the fenced `- /etc/passwd` line is code content too and is not an entry (clause 2). The real `## Files opened` heading opens the block and its single entry matches an allow line (clause 4). No hit.

alt_reading.description: The fenced `# files opened` line is read as a heading, so it opens a block and the fenced `- /etc/passwd` line becomes an entry with no matching allow line.

cases.title: CONTROL: the tool's json-fence protection does not cover the files-opened rule

clauses: 1. A block opens at a Markdown heading (any level) whose text contains `files opened` or `opened files` (case-insensitive), or at a line whose trimmed text starts with `Files opened:` or `Opened files:` (case-insensitive).

2. Entries are the following lines that start (after optional indentation) with `- `, `* `, `+ `, `N. ` or `N) `, or with `|` (a table row); a table's separator row (only `|`, `-`, `:` and spaces) and the row directly above it are not entries. Blank lines inside the block are skipped.

4. An entry's candidates are its tokens, stripped of wrapping backticks, quotes and brackets, trailing `,;.` and a `:L` / `:L-M` suffix, that contain `://`, `/` or `.` or equal `LOG.md`, `SCORECARD.md`, `SKILL.md` or `PROVINCE.md`. An entry with no candidate, or with a candidate no allow line matches, is one `writer-forbidden-opened-path` hit at its own line.
rule_text_reading.reading: A `json` fence inside a `## Cases` section is the shape the tool protects from the two round-30 detectors, but that protection is scoped to the detectors: the files-opened parser still reads the fenced `# files opened` line as a heading, so the fenced `- /etc/passwd` line is an entry with no matching allow line and gives one `writer-forbidden-opened-path` hit at line 5. This control separates "fence-blind" from "json-fence-protected": only the former is what E06 measures.

cases.note: The expected column here is the tool-faithful reading, so agree=yes here is expected by design.
